rules.statement: A name that has served more than one key resolves to the key whose serves interval contains the whole run interval (one interval for all candidates, its lower bound the earliest candidate's release); an interval straddling the switch is ambiguous, never the newer model.
rules.conditions: exactly one candidate's serves interval covers the run interval
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (straddling interval: ambiguous, 22 Oct)

rules.statement: A mode fact (Pro, a request parameter) selects the key its line's models.json modes record at the run date.
rules.conditions: the mode's interval covers the run interval; no router in the chain that cannot separate it (pro-via-router-out)
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: An effort label in other words maps to a configuration when the model's configurations make it unique ("lowest effort setting" on [low ... max] → low).
inputs: models.json configurations at the run date
rules.conditions: unique match; the configuration is served as itself
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: A requested level the maker converts (models.json conversions) is the configuration the maker serves, when the conversion's interval covers the run interval.
rules.conditions: the conversion is dated and covers the run interval (decision-c-conversions-dated)
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews); decision C of the maintainer

rules.statement: Each step of the route chain (harness → router / reseller / host → maker) maps the requested configuration as routes.json documents it at the run date (identity where documented; OpenRouter nearest supported level, ties ambiguous; a router budget → budget-converted); route unknown → every candidate route must agree.
rules.conditions: each mapping's interval covers the run interval
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: No effort sent → the documented default: the maker's on its API or a reseller; a router's or host's own dated default when the run is known to have gone through it.
rules.conditions: the default's interval covers the run interval
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (router clause, 22 Oct: latitude kimi-k3, OpenRouter default_effort max)

rules.statement: A config file's history covering the run interval with the same setting gives that setting for the run.
rules.conditions: the history covers the whole run interval with one setting
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: A source stating that no effort was sent (an effort field null, no reasoning parameter) records no-effort-sent, which step 7 resolves through api-default-documented.
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: A thinking-off statement (reasoning_effort none, enable_thinking false, thinking disabled, a non-reasoning id; spellings in vocab.json nothink_spelling) is the configuration nothink, when it is one of the model's configurations.
rules.conditions: nothink in the model's configurations, served as itself
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: A value that is a mean of runs including a failed run is recomputed from the per-run values with the failed runs excluded; the recomputed mean must reproduce the source's mean on the runs it covers.
rules.conditions: per-run values written
rules.precision: the printed step of the run scores, propagated as a mean
rules.decided_by: the coordinator's answers to the build (commit 06ddbbf), on DATA-PIPELINE §5.2 step 4

rules.statement: A score written as counts (k of n) is put on the percent metric as 100·k/n, exactly.
rules.decided_by: the coordinator's answers to the build (commit 06ddbbf)

rules.statement: For a couple with some components of a linear composite measured, the composite keeps only its residual for the missing components: (composite − Σ present weight·component) / Σ missing weight, on the composite's scale.
rules.conditions: linear true, weights in hand, no normalisation; residuals of an estimated index refused
rules.precision: quadrature of the weighted precisions over the missing weight
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (composite residual rule, 22 Oct)

rules.statement: The publisher's own cost figure is kept when every price that could have applied over the price date equals the base price.
rules.conditions: price date fully covered by registered prices
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: The price change applied to the source's own cost once its formula reproduces it from the run's tokens: cost + Σ tokens × (base − old).
rules.conditions: one price vector over the price date; the formula reproduces the cost within its printed step; long-context tiers only with requests and per-call sizes
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: When the base price is the old price times one factor across every class, the cost is multiplied by that factor.
rules.conditions: the same factor for every class and every price vector over the price date
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: A cost put on a later price by the class-median ratio of the model's measured class shares (METHODOLOGY §2), its spread added to the precision.
rules.conditions: a ratio registered for the model and the setup or measure, price date before its change
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (METHODOLOGY §2; Sonnet 5.5 cache cut of 7 Oct)

rules.statement: A point read off a raster chart takes the chart's calibration and reading sd as its precision.
rules.precision: sd = reading_px × units per px (log axes: on log10)
rules.decided_by: data/README.md, reading precision (September 2026)

rules.statement: A cost's currency is the stated currency fact; costs of different currencies are never mixed in one subset and are re-priced only with prices in that currency.
rules.decided_by: DATA-PIPELINE v3 (22 Oct 2026, after four independent reviews)

rules.statement: A score written as a fraction is put on a percent metric (× 100) and back (÷ 100), exactly; the scale comes from the fact's `scale`, never from the size of the value.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (DATA-PIPELINE 9f3e7ef)

rules.statement: A label that names a level of the model's configurations, served as itself, is that level (LMArena kept).
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: A closed harness (Cursor, Antigravity, Grok CLI, Copilot, Amp, Kiro) that shows a level label without documenting what it sends: the label is the level sent to the maker's API, flagged harness-label-as-level (as LMArena's labels). A documented, dated mapping of the harness wins.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: A route the source does not name is unknown, never presumed to be the maker's API: no route at all, only a harness (the harness applies first, the rest of the chain is unknown), or a named route the registry cannot resolve. Every candidate route (each route of routes.json that served the model at the run date, the maker's API included) is evaluated; the configuration is accepted only if all agree, else not-established:absent. It replaces route-presumed-maker-api (26 Oct).
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: A Pro (or other) mode run through a router that cannot separate it from the base model is out: its model is not established.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: An effort the model's API does not expose takes the level the maker's documented conversion applies, only when the conversion is dated and its interval covers the run (decision C of 20 Oct, commit 7888b85, restated 22 Oct: conversions only when dated).
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (decision C, 20 Oct; restated 22 Oct)

rules.statement: A couple with any component measured loses the composite; a linear composite keeps only its residual for the missing components; a non-linear composite is kept whole only for couples with no component.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: In each part of a setup's costs (basis × method × unit × currency × route), the re-priced measures form one subset; an unrepriced cost stays only as a price band toward the base (current) price (cost-price-band, own subset per model; cost-current-price-only, the maintainer, 3 Nov 2026: every cost of the fit at the current price, the band's reference always the base price); the others are out:cost-not-comparable (until 3 Nov a model whose price change over the price-date interval was uniform across classes formed its own subset at its old price, and a band's reference was the last price seen).
inputs: cost basis, method, unit, currency, route
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: A score at the floor or the ceiling of its metric for one couple while the others are not is left out (out:uninformative); its cost is kept.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (METHODOLOGY §2, method of 29 Sep 2026)

rules.statement: Each model has its own list of configurations; every configuration of the list enters the fit as its own couple (low … max, minimal, nothink, think, solo), except think-<budget> (out:budget-config) and the terms vocab.json marks in_fit false (between-tools); solo only for a model whose list is [solo]. A method change: before/after before main.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: For a source whose cost method is found neither in its documentation nor by reproducing its costs from its tokens, one table of one source is taken as one method (cost_method_unstated = single-per-table, flag cost-method-assumed-single).
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: For a retired model the base price is its last list price.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (decision 1 of 21 Oct)

rules.statement: For a model whose standard price never applied before it was withdrawn, the base price is the price actually charged (Gemini 3.7 Flash, $0.75).
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: A model's documented default identical on both sides of a span without captures covers the span: only between two default records of the same model and setting giving the same configuration, when no other record of that setting states another configuration inside the span and no name of the model (any route) starts or ends inside it. The span's basis is `bridged`; the measures it decides carry the flag default-bridged. The same rule applies to a route's own defaults for a model (the maintainer, 3 Nov 2026: OpenRouter's catalogue defaults), records of one setting and one via; a route id of the model starting or ending inside the span also forbids the bridge.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (29 Oct: qwen3.6-plus, think before 21 May and after 19 Oct)

rules.statement: A cost whose price date no registered price covers is re-priced from the class prices the source states it applied (price-table facts whose term is a price class) to the registered base price, as a registered price vector would be (the publisher's figure, the delta on its tokens, a uniform factor); equal prices give factor 1. It needs a registered base price.
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (29 Oct: 'if the source gives the price, where is the problem?')

rules.statement: A cost that stays unrepriced only because its long-context tiers cannot be resolved (requests and per-call sizes not stated) is re-priced when every price vector over its price date relates to the base vector by one common factor on every class it can have used (the classes and long-context tiers of the base vector; the tiers the same on both sides): cost × that factor, whatever the token mix. It joins the part's re-priced subset instead of a subset of its own model. Several vectors at different factors, or a change in some classes only, keep the unrepriced path (own subset, cost-price-band).
rules.conditions: the same factor for every class and tier of the base vector and every price vector over the price date; a promotion is never the base
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (30 Oct: GPT-5.6 Luna and Terra on OpenAI's launch page, 80 % and 20 % less from 30 Jul on every class)
rules.ref: data/BUILD.md, Added on 30 Oct; docs/DATA-PIPELINE.md §5.3 step 1

rules.statement: A router serving the model at the run date (OpenRouter) accepts the levels of the maker's API at that date and passes them on unchanged, besides the levels its own catalogue lists; only a conversion its documents establish for that model (a model mapping) changes the level. A generic sentence (OpenRouter's effort → budget_tokens formula for 'Anthropic models') applies only to the models it covers: the Claude models that take a thinking budget and no effort.
rules.conditions: the accepts_maker record covers the run interval; the route's ids for the model overlap it; the route's catalogue lists no level of the model over the run (else router-listed-levels; the maintainer, 3 Nov 2026, later)
rules.decided_by: the maintainer

rules.statement: Where a router's catalogue lists the model's levels at the run date (OpenRouter's supported_efforts in /api/v1/models, recorded as level accepts), its list decides what the router accepts: a level it does not list falls to the router's level_mapping (nearest supported, a tie → ambiguous). The maker's levels (router-maker-levels) count only where the catalogue lists no level of the model at that date. A run the listing covers in part is read both ways and kept only if both agree.
rules.conditions: the router has a covering accepts_maker record; level accepts records of the model overlap the run
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (3 Nov 2026: glm-5.2 max, which OpenRouter lists as xhigh / high / none)

rules.statement: The router's catalogue listing (router-listed-levels) decides thinking off and on as well as the levels: thinking off is accepted only where the listing names it (OpenRouter's supported_efforts « none »); where the listing does not, thinking off asked for follows the router's level_mapping (nearest supported, thinking off being the lowest step of the order, a tie → ambiguous), thinking off asked for a model that has no thinking off at its maker is not established (no nearest level: kimi-k3, the maintainer, 3 Nov 2026, later); thinking on without a level, which the listing never names, is accepted where the listing names at least one level (the maintainer, 3 Nov 2026, later). The maker's thinking off / on count only where the catalogue lists nothing for the model at that date.
inputs: routes.json accepts (levels and nothink from supported_efforts), level_mapping
rules.conditions: as router-listed-levels; the configuration asked for is nothink or think
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (3 Nov 2026: gpt-5.5 nothink; OpenRouter lists « none » for most models only from 15 Oct 2026)

rules.statement: A harness that hands every call to one route (Claude Code → the Anthropic API, maker-api) closes the chain with that route when the measure names no other route: no other candidate route is weighed.
rules.conditions: every harness named has a calls_route naming the same route; the route slot names no router, reseller, host or self-hosting
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (3 Nov 2026: Claude Code goes directly to Anthropic)

rules.statement: A harness whose calls always go through a library or proxy route has that route as a step of every chain it is in, right after it (OpenHands → LiteLLM): the route then applies as any named step; a route documenting nothing (LiteLLM) leaves the run not established (strict rule).
rules.conditions: the harness is a step of the measure's chain (named in its route slot) and carries passes_through
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (3 Nov 2026: LiteLLM is in the chain of every OpenHands source, its SDK calling the providers through the LiteLLM library)

rules.statement: The effort facts of a measure are reconciled first on what they read (the configuration each asks for, before any route step: a setting, a label, thinking off / on, a budget, the name), with the same rules as after the route (a level beside thinking on → the level; the more specific statement of the same call; a reading outside the model's configurations counts for nothing beside one inside). Readings that still disagree make the configuration not-established:contradictory, whatever the route then serves; a reading the route no longer serves does not leave the other one alone.
inputs: effort facts (effort-setting, effort-label, thinking-on / -off, thinking-budget, effort-order, name)
rules.conditions: two or more effort readings of one measure
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (3 Nov 2026: Artificial Analysis opus-4.7 / sonnet-5, facts thinking off and high; thinking off no longer served through OpenRouter)

rules.statement: A cost that none of the re-pricing rules (publisher figure, delta on the source's tokens, uniform factor, uniform factor across tiers, class ratio) brings to the base price is brought to it by a price band when every price over its price date is registered and shares the base price's classes and long-context tiers: the band [raw × the smallest, raw × the largest per-class ratio base / old] over its own price vectors (the bounds « mostly input » and « mostly output »), its reference always the base (current) price, never the last price seen (the maintainer, 3 Nov 2026, later: « les fourchettes de prix se calculent vers le prix courant »; GPT-5.6 Sol, base 5 / 30, promotion 4 / 20 over the price date: × [1.25, 1.5]). A cost no band can bring to the current price (no registered price over its price date, or tiers / classes not shared) is out:cost-not-comparable. The unrepriced model's own subset at an old price no longer exists.
inputs: cost field (price vectors over the price date, base price)
rules.conditions: a cost not re-priced
rules.decided_by: the maintainer (3 Nov 2026: Sonnet 5.5 launch page, Terminal-Bench 4.0 costs at the 28 Sep price; cache read 0.20 → 0.10 on 7 Oct)
rules.ref: data/BUILD.md Interpretations 30; Added on 3 Nov 2026 (route5) 7, (route6) 2; docs/DATA-PIPELINE.md §5.3 step 2
